header.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). A28 ways from an Overpass extract, OSM base 2026-05-03T12:53:56Z (manus-output/birchie-osm/birchington.json, not in git), projected as tools/osm-to-svg.py does.
header.edgeKey: edge = index into the graph's edges array; nodes = that entry's [i, j] as written
header.method: Each trunk edge is sampled at 5 points and matched to the OSM A28 way with the smallest mean distance. kind: dual = one-way carriageways west of Brooksend (the real 1.7 km, 50 mph); divided = every other one-way pair (Birchington to Westgate, and the 0.14 km refuge split at Westgate); single = two-way. oneway = the OSM direction of the carriageway the edge lies on, as [from, to], null where OSM is two-way. matchM = mean distance to that way.
header.warning: The game graph draws each dual or divided stretch as one line that keeps to one carriageway, with short side-loops onto the other; it does not have both carriageways end to end. Applying oneway edge by edge makes those stretches one-directional for cars (see checks). For routing, treat trunk edges as two-way; use kind, maxspeedMph and lanes for drawing and speed.
